what_its_for: Tolcapone is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It is used together with two other medicines called levodopa and carbidopa. Tolcapone helps levodopa work better and longer in your body, which helps reduce the 'wearing-off' periods when your Parkinson's symptoms come back between doses.
how_to_take: Take tolcapone exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Always take it along with your levodopa/carbidopa medicine — do not take tolcapone alone. Take it 3 times a day: the first dose in the morning at the same time as your first levodopa/carbidopa dose, then again about 6 hours later, and then 6 hours after that.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg taken 3 times a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 200 mg three times a day if needed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Because tolcapone can cause serious liver problems, your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your liver while you are on this medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tolcapone at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking tolcapone, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Be careful when driving, using machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert, because tolcapone may cause dizziness or sudden sleepiness. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause a drop in blood pressure and make you feel faint. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, as tolcapone can interact with many medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, loss of appetite, or nausea — these could be signs of serious liver damage. Also call your doctor if you experience: unusual or uncontrollable movements of your body (dyskinesia), confusion, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), high fever with muscle stiffness and confusion (a rare but serious reaction called neuroleptic malignant syndrome), very low blood pressure or fainting, or the urge to gamble, eat, spend money, or have sex in ways that are unusual for you.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in your Parkinson's symptoms — such as smoother movement and fewer 'off' periods — within a few days to a couple of weeks of starting tolcapone. However, it may take a little longer to see the full benefit. Keep taking the medicine as directed even if you do not notice changes right away. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and hallucinations. Use with caution and follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of tolcapone during pregnancy is not well established. Breastfeeding: It is not known if tolcapone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver disease: Tolcapone should NOT be used if you have liver disease or have had liver problems in the past. Your doctor will monitor your liver with regular blood tests. Kidney disease: Use with caution if you have kidney problems; your doctor may need to adjust your treatment.
